# RAG Patterns

Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) combines a retriever (finding relevant documents) with a generator (LLM that answers using those documents). This guide covers four RAG architectures, from simplest to most advanced.

---

## Why RAG?

LLMs have fixed training data. RAG lets you:
- Answer questions about your own documents
- Cite sources
- Reduce hallucinations
- Update knowledge without retraining

---

## Pattern Overview

| Pattern | How it works | When to use |
|---|---|---|
| **Basic RAG** | Retrieve → Generate | Simple Q&A over a document set |
| **Adaptive RAG** | Decide if retrieval is needed, then retrieve | Mixed questions (some need docs, some do not) |
| **Corrective RAG** | Retrieve, grade results, rewrite query if needed | High-accuracy requirements |
| **Self-RAG** | Grade retrieval, grade generation, retry | Maximum accuracy, self-correction |

---

## Building Blocks

All RAG patterns share these components. You write them in R — no external vector database required for prototyping.

### Simple retriever (keyword-based)

```r
#' Create a keyword-based retriever from a character vector of documents
#' @param corpus Character vector of documents
#' @return A function(query, k) that returns the top-k matching documents
create_keyword_retriever <- function(corpus) {
  function(query, k = 3) {
    # Tokenize the query
    words <- tolower(strsplit(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9 ]", " ", query), "\\s+")[[1]])
    words <- words[nchar(words) > 2]

    # Score each document by keyword overlap
    scores <- vapply(corpus, function(doc) {
      doc_lower <- tolower(doc)
      sum(vapply(words, function(w) grepl(w, doc_lower, fixed = TRUE), logical(1)))
    }, numeric(1))

    # Return top-k
    idx <- order(scores, decreasing = TRUE)
    idx <- idx[scores[idx] > 0]
    head(idx, k)
  }
}
```

### TF-IDF retriever (better quality)

```r
#' Create a TF-IDF retriever
#' @param corpus Character vector of documents
#' @return A function(query, k) that returns top-k document indices
create_tfidf_retriever <- function(corpus) {
  # Build the vocabulary
  docs_tokens <- strsplit(tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9 ]", " ", corpus)), "\\s+")
  vocab <- unique(unlist(docs_tokens))
  vocab <- vocab[nchar(vocab) > 2]

  # Compute document frequency
  df <- vapply(vocab, function(term) {
    sum(vapply(docs_tokens, function(tokens) term %in% tokens, logical(1)))
  }, numeric(1))

  # Compute IDF
  n_docs <- length(corpus)
  idf <- log(n_docs / df)

  # Compute TF-IDF vectors for each document
  doc_vectors <- lapply(docs_tokens, function(tokens) {
    tf <- table(factor(tokens[tokens %in% vocab], levels = vocab))
    as.numeric(tf) * idf
  })

  # Return retriever function
  function(query, k = 3) {
    query_tokens <- strsplit(tolower(gsub("[^A-Za-z0-9 ]", " ", query)), "\\s+")[[1]]
    query_tf <- table(factor(query_tokens[query_tokens %in% vocab], levels = vocab))
    query_vec <- as.numeric(query_tf) * idf

    # Cosine similarity
    scores <- vapply(doc_vectors, function(doc_vec) {
      sum(query_vec * doc_vec) / (sqrt(sum(query_vec^2)) * sqrt(sum(doc_vec^2)) + 1e-10)
    }, numeric(1))

    idx <- order(scores, decreasing = TRUE)
    idx <- idx[scores[idx] > 0]
    head(idx, k)
  }
}
```

### Embedding-based retriever (best quality)

If you have an embedding model available, use cosine similarity on embeddings:

```r
#' Create an embedding-based retriever using lg_call_model for embeddings
#' @param corpus Character vector of documents
#' @return A function(query, k) that returns top-k document indices
create_embedding_retriever <- function(corpus) {
  # Compute embeddings for all documents
  # This uses lg_call_model if your provider supports embeddings,
  # or falls back to a hash-based pseudo-embedding for prototyping
  doc_embeddings <- lapply(corpus, function(doc) {
    # Simple hash-based embedding (replace with real embeddings in production)
    words <- strsplit(tolower(doc), "\\W+")[[1]]
    words <- words[nchar(words) > 0]
    vec <- rep(0, 100)
    for (w in words) {
      hash <- sum(charToRaw(w)) %% 100 + 1
      vec[hash] <- vec[hash] + 1
    }
    vec / (sqrt(sum(vec^2)) + 1e-10)
  })

  function(query, k = 3) {
    # Embed the query
    words <- strsplit(tolower(query), "\\W+")[[1]]
    words <- words[nchar(words) > 0]
    query_vec <- rep(0, 100)
    for (w in words) {
      hash <- sum(charToRaw(w)) %% 100 + 1
      query_vec[hash] <- query_vec[hash] + 1
    }
    query_vec <- query_vec / (sqrt(sum(query_vec^2)) + 1e-10)

    # Cosine similarity
    scores <- sapply(doc_embeddings, function(doc_vec) {
      sum(query_vec * doc_vec)
    })

    head(order(scores, decreasing = TRUE), k)
  }
}
```

### Document store with metadata

```r
#' Create a document store
#' @param documents List of lists with $text and $metadata
create_doc_store <- function(documents) {
  list(
    docs = documents,
    texts = sapply(documents, function(d) d$text),
    add = function(doc) {
      documents <<- c(documents, list(doc))
    },
    get_all = function() documents,
    get_text = function() sapply(documents, function(d) d$text)
  )
}
```

## 1. Basic RAG

Retrieve documents, stuff them into the prompt, generate an answer. The simplest effective RAG.

```r
library(langgraphr)

# Sample corpus
corpus <- c(
  "langgraphr lets R developers build AI agents on the LangGraph engine.",
  "lg_connect() gives an assistant whose tools are R functions.",
  "lg_graph(), lg_add_node() and lg_compile() build stateful R-node graphs.",
  "Thread memory persists across calls; lg_use_sqlite() makes it durable.",
  "lg_call_model() calls an OpenAI-compatible model directly from R.",
  "The hidden server uses FastAPI and uvicorn to run LangGraph in Python."
)

retriever <- create_tfidf_retriever(corpus)

basic_rag <- lg_graph("basic_rag",
  state = list(
    question = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    context_docs = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

retrieve_node <- function(state) {
  idx <- retriever(state$input, k = 2)
  docs <- if (length(idx) > 0) corpus[idx] else character(0)

  list(
    updates = list(
      question = state$input,
      context_docs = docs
    ),
    goto = "generate"
  )
}

generate_node <- function(state) {
  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")

  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Answer the question using ONLY the context below.",
      "If the context is insufficient, say 'I don't have enough information.'",
      "\n\nContext:\n", context
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))

  list(updates = list(answer = answer))
}

rag_graph <- basic_rag |>
  lg_add_node("retrieve", retrieve_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate", generate_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("retrieve", "generate") |>
  lg_compile()

result <- rag_graph$invoke("How do I build a graph in R?")
result$state$answer
result$state$context_docs  # see which docs were retrieved
```

### With citations

```r
generate_with_citations <- function(state) {
  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")

  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Answer using ONLY the context below.",
      "After each claim, cite the source as [Doc N] where N is the document number.",
      "If the context is insufficient, say so.",
      "\n\nContext:\n",
      paste(paste0("[Doc ", seq_along(state$context_docs), "] ",
                   state$context_docs), collapse = "\n\n")
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))

  list(updates = list(answer = answer))
}
```

## 2. Adaptive RAG

Not every question needs retrieval. "What is 2+2?" does not need a document lookup. Adaptive RAG decides whether to retrieve before answering.

```r
adaptive_rag <- lg_graph("adaptive_rag",
  state = list(
    question = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    needs_retrieval = list(type = "boolean", reducer = "overwrite"),
    context_docs = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Decision node: does this question need document retrieval?
assess_node <- function(state) {
  decision <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Determine if the question requires looking up external documents.",
      "Questions about specific documents, policies, or proprietary information: YES",
      "General knowledge, math, or opinions: NO",
      "Respond with only YES or NO."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$input)
  ), temperature = 0)

  needs <- grepl("YES", decision, ignore.case = TRUE)

  list(
    updates = list(
      question = state$input,
      needs_retrieval = needs
    ),
    goto = if (needs) "retrieve" else "generate_direct"
  )
}

retrieve_node <- function(state) {
  idx <- retriever(state$question, k = 3)
  docs <- if (length(idx) > 0) corpus[idx] else character(0)
  list(updates = list(context_docs = docs), goto = "generate_with_context")
}

generate_with_context_node <- function(state) {
  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste("Answer using this context:\n\n", context)),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))
  list(updates = list(answer = answer))
}

generate_direct_node <- function(state) {
  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = "You are a helpful assistant."),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))
  list(updates = list(answer = answer))
}

rag_graph <- adaptive_rag |>
  lg_add_node("assess", assess_node) |>
  lg_add_node("retrieve", retrieve_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate_with_context", generate_with_context_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate_direct", generate_direct_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("assess", "retrieve") |>
  lg_add_edge("retrieve", "generate_with_context") |>
  lg_compile()

# Questions that need retrieval
r1 <- rag_graph$invoke("What does lg_connect() do?")

# Questions that do not need retrieval
r2 <- rag_graph$invoke("What is the capital of France?")
```

## 3. Corrective RAG (CRAG)

Retrieve, then grade the retrieved documents. If they are not relevant, rewrite the query and try again. Only generate when you have good context.

```r
crag <- lg_graph("crag",
  state = list(
    question = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    context_docs = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    doc_grade = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
    rewritten_query = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    retry_count = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
    answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

retrieve_node <- function(state) {
  query <- state$rewritten_query %||% state$input
  idx <- retriever(query, k = 3)
  docs <- if (length(idx) > 0) corpus[idx] else character(0)
  list(
    updates = list(
      question = state$input,
      context_docs = docs,
      rewritten_query = query
    ),
    goto = "grade"
  )
}

# Grade the retrieved documents
grade_node <- function(state) {
  if (length(state$context_docs) == 0) {
    return(list(updates = list(doc_grade = 0), goto = "rewrite"))
  }

  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  grade <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Grade the relevance of these documents to the question.",
      "Respond with only a number 1-10.",
      "10 = perfectly relevant, 1 = completely irrelevant."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Question: ", state$question,
      "\n\nDocuments:\n", context
    ))
  ), temperature = 0)

  score <- as.numeric(trimws(grade))
  if (is.na(score)) score <- 5

  retries <- state$retry_count %||% 0

  # If documents are good enough, generate. If not, rewrite and retry.
  goto <- if (score >= 6 || retries >= 2) "generate" else "rewrite"

  list(updates = list(doc_grade = score, retry_count = retries), goto = goto)
}

# Rewrite the query for better retrieval
rewrite_node <- function(state) {
  rewritten <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Rewrite the question to improve document retrieval.",
      "Use different keywords, synonyms, or rephrase.",
      "Return ONLY the rewritten question, nothing else."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))

  retries <- (state$retry_count %||% 0) + 1

  list(
    updates = list(rewritten_query = trimws(rewritten), retry_count = retries),
    goto = "retrieve"
  )
}

# Generate the answer with good context
generate_node <- function(state) {
  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")

  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Answer the question using the context.",
      "If the context does not fully answer the question, acknowledge the gap.",
      "\n\nContext:\n", context
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))

  list(updates = list(answer = answer))
}

rag_graph <- crag |>
  lg_add_node("retrieve", retrieve_node) |>
  lg_add_node("grade", grade_node) |>
  lg_add_node("rewrite", rewrite_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate", generate_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("retrieve", "grade") |>
  lg_add_edge("grade", "rewrite") |>
  lg_add_edge("rewrite", "retrieve") |>
  lg_compile()

result <- rag_graph$invoke("How does memory persistence work?")
result$state$answer
result$state$doc_grade        # quality of retrieved docs
result$state$retry_count       # how many query rewrites
result$state$rewritten_query   # final query used
```

## 4. Self-RAG

The most advanced pattern. The LLM grades its own retrieval, decides to generate, then grades its own answer — retrying at each stage if quality is low.

```r
self_rag <- lg_graph("self_rag",
  state = list(
    question = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    context_docs = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
    retrieval_grade = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),  # "relevant" or "irrelevant"
    answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
    generation_grade = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),  # "grounded" or "not_grounded"
    useful = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),            # "useful" or "not_useful"
    retry_count = list(type = "number", reducer = "overwrite"),
    final_answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
  ))

# Step 1: Retrieve documents
retrieve_node <- function(state) {
  idx <- retriever(state$input, k = 3)
  docs <- if (length(idx) > 0) corpus[idx] else character(0)
  list(
    updates = list(question = state$input, context_docs = docs),
    goto = "grade_retrieval"
  )
}

# Step 2: Grade whether the retrieved docs are relevant
grade_retrieval_node <- function(state) {
  if (length(state$context_docs) == 0) {
    return(list(updates = list(retrieval_grade = "irrelevant"), goto = "decide_generate"))
  }

  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  grade <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Are these documents relevant to the question?",
      "Respond with ONLY 'relevant' or 'irrelevant'."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Question: ", state$question,
      "\n\nDocuments:\n", context
    ))
  ), temperature = 0)

  grade <- trimws(tolower(grade))
  if (!grade %in% c("relevant", "irrelevant")) grade <- "irrelevant"

  list(updates = list(retrieval_grade = grade), goto = "decide_generate")
}

# Step 3: Decide whether to generate (relevant docs) or generate without (irrelevant)
decide_generate_node <- function(state) {
  goto <- if (identical(state$retrieval_grade, "relevant")) {
    "generate_with_context"
  } else {
    "generate_without_context"
  }
  list(goto = goto)
}

# Step 4a: Generate with context
generate_with_context_node <- function(state) {
  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste("Answer using this context:\n\n", context)),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))
  list(updates = list(answer = answer), goto = "grade_generation")
}

# Step 4b: Generate without context (retrieval found nothing useful)
generate_without_context_node <- function(state) {
  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "No relevant documents were found.",
      "Answer from your own knowledge, but note that you lack supporting documents."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ))
  list(updates = list(answer = answer), goto = "grade_generation")
}

# Step 5: Grade whether the answer is grounded in the context
grade_generation_node <- function(state) {
  # If there was no context, skip grounding check
  if (length(state$context_docs) == 0) {
    return(list(updates = list(generation_grade = "no_context"), goto = "check_useful"))
  }

  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  grade <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Is the answer grounded in and supported by the context?",
      "Respond with ONLY 'grounded' or 'not_grounded'."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Context:\n", context,
      "\n\nAnswer: ", state$answer
    ))
  ), temperature = 0)

  grade <- trimws(tolower(grade))
  if (!grade %in% c("grounded", "not_grounded")) grade <- "not_grounded"

  list(
    updates = list(generation_grade = grade),
    goto = if (grade == "grounded") "check_useful" else "regenerate"
  )
}

# Step 5b: Regenerate if not grounded
regenerate_node <- function(state) {
  retries <- (state$retry_count %||% 0) + 1
  if (retries >= 2) {
    return(list(updates = list(retry_count = retries), goto = "check_useful"))
  }

  context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n")
  answer <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Your previous answer was not grounded in the context.",
      "Rewrite your answer using ONLY information from the context.",
      "\n\nContext:\n", context
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = state$question)
  ), temperature = 0.3)

  list(
    updates = list(answer = answer, retry_count = retries),
    goto = "grade_generation"
  )
}

# Step 6: Check if the answer is useful to the user
check_useful_node <- function(state) {
  useful <- lg_call_model(list(
    list(role = "system", content = paste(
      "Is this answer useful for the user's question?",
      "Respond with ONLY 'useful' or 'not_useful'."
    )),
    list(role = "user", content = paste0(
      "Question: ", state$question,
      "\n\nAnswer: ", state$answer
    ))
  ), temperature = 0)

  useful <- trimws(tolower(useful))
  if (!useful %in% c("useful", "not_useful")) useful <- "useful"

  list(updates = list(useful = useful, final_answer = state$answer))
}

rag_graph <- self_rag |>
  lg_add_node("retrieve", retrieve_node) |>
  lg_add_node("grade_retrieval", grade_retrieval_node) |>
  lg_add_node("decide_generate", decide_generate_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate_with_context", generate_with_context_node) |>
  lg_add_node("generate_without_context", generate_without_context_node) |>
  lg_add_node("grade_generation", grade_generation_node) |>
  lg_add_node("regenerate", regenerate_node) |>
  lg_add_node("check_useful", check_useful_node) |>
  lg_add_edge("grade_generation", "regenerate") |>
  lg_add_edge("regenerate", "grade_generation") |>
  lg_compile()

result <- rag_graph$invoke("How do I persist conversation memory?")
result$state$final_answer
result$state$retrieval_grade    # "relevant" or "irrelevant"
result$state$generation_grade   # "grounded" or "not_grounded"
result$state$useful              # "useful" or "not_useful"
```

## RAG with File Loading

Here is a complete RAG system that loads documents from files:

```r
#' Load documents from a directory
#' @param dir_path Path to a directory with .txt, .md, or .csv files
#' @return Character vector of document texts
load_documents <- function(dir_path) {
  files <- list.files(dir_path, pattern = "\\.(txt|md|csv)$",
                      full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)

  docs <- lapply(files, function(f) {
    ext <- tolower(tools::file_ext(f))
    if (ext == "csv") {
      df <- read.csv(f)
      paste(names(df), collapse = ", ")
    } else {
      paste(readLines(f, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
    }
  })

  unlist(docs)
}

#' Build a complete RAG system from a directory of documents
#' @param dir_path Path to documents
#' @return A compiled LgGraph
build_rag_from_dir <- function(dir_path) {
  corpus <- load_documents(dir_path)
  retriever <- create_tfidf_retriever(corpus)

  rag <- lg_graph("file_rag",
    state = list(
      question = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite"),
      context_docs = list(type = "list", reducer = "overwrite"),
      answer = list(type = "str", reducer = "overwrite")
    ))

  rag <- lg_add_node(rag, "retrieve", function(state) {
    idx <- retriever(state$input, k = 3)
    docs <- if (length(idx) > 0) corpus[idx] else character(0)
    list(updates = list(question = state$input, context_docs = docs), goto = "generate")
  })

  rag <- lg_add_node(rag, "generate", function(state) {
    context <- paste(state$context_docs, collapse = "\n\n---\n\n")
    answer <- lg_call_model(list(
      list(role = "system", content = paste(
        "Answer the question using the provided documents.",
        "Cite sources by document number.",
        "\n\nDocuments:\n", context
      )),
      list(role = "user", content = state$question)
    ))
    list(updates = list(answer = answer))
  })

  lg_add_edge(rag, "retrieve", "generate") |> lg_compile()
}

# Usage
# rag_system <- build_rag_from_dir("my_documents")
# result <- rag_system$invoke("What is the refund policy?")
```

## Chunking Strategies

For long documents, split them into chunks before indexing:

```r
#' Split a long text into overlapping chunks
#' @param text Character string
#' @param chunk_size Maximum characters per chunk
#' @param overlap Overlap between chunks
#' @return Character vector of chunks
chunk_text <- function(text, chunk_size = 500, overlap = 50) {
  n <- nchar(text)
  if (n <= chunk_size) return(text)

  chunks <- c()
  start <- 1
  while (start <= n) {
    end <- min(start + chunk_size - 1, n)
    chunks <- c(chunks, substr(text, start, end))
    start <- end - overlap + 1
  }
  chunks
}

#' Chunk and index a directory of files
#' @param dir_path Path to documents
#' @return List with $corpus (chunks) and $retriever (function)
build_chunked_index <- function(dir_path, chunk_size = 500) {
  files <- list.files(dir_path, pattern = "\\.(txt|md)$",
                      full.names = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)

  all_chunks <- c()
  chunk_meta <- list()  # track which file each chunk came from

  for (f in files) {
    text <- paste(readLines(f, warn = FALSE), collapse = "\n")
    chunks <- chunk_text(text, chunk_size = chunk_size)
    all_chunks <- c(all_chunks, chunks)
    for (i in seq_along(chunks)) {
      chunk_meta[[length(chunk_meta) + 1]] <- list(
        file = basename(f),
        chunk = i,
        text = chunks[i]
      )
    }
  }

  retriever <- create_tfidf_retriever(all_chunks)

  list(
    corpus = all_chunks,
    meta = chunk_meta,
    retriever = retriever
  )
}
```

## Choosing a RAG Pattern

| Your situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Simple Q&A, small corpus | Basic RAG |
| Mixed questions (some general, some specific) | Adaptive RAG |
| Need high accuracy, have noisy docs | Corrective RAG |
| Maximum accuracy, willing to pay for extra LLM calls | Self-RAG |
| Have many large files | Chunk + Basic RAG |
| Need to cite sources | Basic RAG with citation prompt |
